items.title: Actual isolation for generated source
items.scope: Linux runner with unprivileged user namespaces (CI sets kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0)
items.notes: Generated specs run only inside user/mount/net/pid/ipc/uts namespaces as an unprivileged user: pivot_root onto a tmpfs root with read-only system binds, the work directory as the only writable host path, loopback-only networking with a relay to the application under test, zero capabilities with no_new_privs, rlimits and a process-group kill on timeout. No host fallback. A TypeScript AST allow-list lint rejects the audit spec and its re-spellings before anything runs. Memory is not cgroup-limited (documented residual).

items.title: Enforced autonomy modes, calibration and resolved-model identity
items.notes: Modes shadow / heuristic_staging / calibrated. items.title: Combined cancellation and real deadlines
items.notes: Every provider call combines the caller signal with its own timeout (AbortSignal.any), caps request/response bytes, retries only network/408/429/5xx with jittered backoff honouring Retry-After, and stops on cancellation. Each attempt has one signal (run cancellation plus wall-clock deadline) passed to S1, S2 and adapter calls.

items.title: Durable pre-dispatch intents and effect reconciliation
items.notes: PREPARED and DISPATCHING are written (fenced) before input. A worker process group killed with SIGKILL mid-checkout is recovered: the intent is reconciled from the application by idempotency key (RECONCILED, one receipt, one order), the shard reruns with a fresh fixture, and the orphan fixture is swept. items.title: Uncertain effects are obligations that hold the gate and promotion
items.scope: intents, shard worker, aggregation, gate, promotion, demo
items.notes: ACKNOWLEDGED mutations are reconciled on recovery (keyed: looked up; unkeyed: review) and SETTLED only when their attempt ends under the live lease. items.external_prerequisite: A delegated kernel cgroup (QA_SANDBOX_CGROUP: cgroup v2 with memory and pids in cgroup.subtree_control, or the v1 memory hierarchy) wherever generated specs are validated; without one, validation errors instead of running

items.title: Sandbox resource contract: required memory and swap bounds enforced or execution refused

history.observed: cgroup v1 host: a denied write, and a weaker read-back, of memory.memsw.limit_in_bytes both left the program running

items.external_prerequisite: A delegated kernel cgroup (see MEM); resource-pressure evidence only on disposable supported workers
items.scope: packages/compiler cgroup factory, sandbox gate, generated-spec validation
items.notes: Contract: resident memory plus swap of the whole tree within the limit — v2 memory.swap.max=0, v1 memory.memsw.limit_in_bytes = limit, or no host swap when the kernel has no swap accounting; each bound written and read back, else refused with a typed reason (control_write_failed, limit_mismatch, swap_unbounded, controller_missing, invalid_config, membership_unverified). Process cap: cgroup pids.max read back where available; v1 without a pids hierarchy records RLIMIT_NPROC (per user), never presented as a cgroup cap. Invalid numeric configuration (including QA_SANDBOX_MEMORY_MB) is an error, not a default.
